author: Claude (Opus 5.5), at the architect's request; awaiting architect review
basis: Organizing idea read from the 15 archive names and concepts exactly as shown to the LLM in Pilot 4 (E01-E15). Grouped before the E-to-archive-id mapping or any neighbourhood result was looked at. Caveat: Claude had earlier seen data/directions.json, which lists bge-m3 clusters by archive id (R*-S*), but not their E numbers.

F1_commons_heart.idea: The commons/hall is the hub; two wings attach only to it, so all movement passes through the shared heart.

F2_civic_hinge_chain.idea: A linear chain: learning at one end, hall at the other, and a public front (civic hinge or gateway) between them that every passage crosses.

F3_linked_cluster_around_court.idea: Three masses each joined to both others, closing a compact triangle or ring around a court, typically with a loft over the commons.

F4_detached_campus.idea: Freestanding buildings on shared grounds: the hall (and sometimes more) stands apart and is reached outdoors.

F5_one_block_service_hinge.idea: One large learning block holds almost the whole day; a low workshop/service pavilion is the hinge to the hall.

F6_low_learning_civic_tower.idea: Classrooms kept low beside a three-storey civic tower that stacks the front, specialist support and library as a vertical marker.

borderline.E09: Placed in F3 for its court loop; its own emphasis (tall academy plus a care-and-making house) could make it a separate idea.
borderline.E10: Placed in F4 for its freestanding hall; its two joined bars could make it a separate idea.
borderline.E04: Placed alone; by diagram it is a chain through a hinge (like F2), and by idea it shares 'one block holds the day' with E14 (F4).
